summary: Cold read of the recorded assistant-ask-surfaces contract and task plan (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only, task-mty7tpi3-ahj3yc) returned NOT CONVERGED with five repository blockers and two product-shape questions; a third question - whether a model id would exist for the live Success check - was carried by the orchestrator from the plan gate. All five blockers were verified against the repo and folded in; all three questions were put to the human in one round. Required leaves rose from eight to ten and write_scope from ten paths to fourteen.

criteria_map.Both surfaces exist and match the approv: Surfaces and navigation. The cold read found app-shell.tsx:15 renders Ask as a DISABLED nav item while the prototype makes it a destination, and that the contract never said what 'Open in Ask' does to the active thread. Ask is now a live shell destination, and the human chose to carry the thread in in-memory app state across that internal navigation - never storage, never a reload - so the control expands the conversation instead of discarding it.
criteria_map.A successful answer renders its title, i: Rendering and charts. The cold read found decision 0007 names recharts for charts while frontend/package.json has no such dependency and neither it nor the lockfile was in scope. Both are now in scope, with an honest-fallback rule: any chartType the client cannot draw truthfully falls back to the table rather than to a misleading chart.
criteria_map.View in report renders from the response: View in report, both sides. The cold read found the stale-link proof misplaced: frontend/src/lib/api.ts:102 still types runMisStatement as MisStatementRunResponse rather than the MisStatementRouteResponse task 1 introduced, so a refresh-required answer would reach StatementView missing fields it reads. The client type widens, mis-report-view.tsx branches, and the required leaf moved to mis-report-view.test.tsx where it can actually prove the route parsed and posted the server-supplied selectors.
criteria_map.All SEVEN ResponseClass values render ho: The seven response classes. The cold read found they do NOT share a shape: an informational answer spreads title, definition and suggestedQuestions with NO message (chat.service.ts:115,125), so a renderer keyed on message alone would show a blank answer or invite the client to invent one. Informational, clarification and the four message-bearing failures are now handled separately.
criteria_map.The client sends only what the contract: Prior turns and the client body. The cold read found AskPriorTurn requires a selection (contract/src/api.ts:122), which only a SUCCESSFUL answer supplies, so the hook must never invent one for a clarification or error turn. The api-client leaf now asserts the exact request body rather than merely the absence of conversationId.
criteria_map.The surfaces are proven by vitest leaves: Proofs and the seeded chips. Required leaves rose from eight to ten. The human chose 3F-specific seed prompts over generic ones, so the criterion binds them to the REGISTERED CATALOG - the governed-financial and mis-statement measures over the DUB slice - because a seeded chip that returns unsupported reads as the product being broken, which is the risk that choice carries. The live Success check is expected to run for real: BEDROCK_MODEL_ID is now configured and a Bedrock call was verified to return a selection.

current_flow: Task 1 registered and governed POST /api/chat and /api/chat/stream and shipped the answer contract, including the required viewInReport discriminated union and the statement route's pinned-batch validation with its typed refresh-required outcome. Nothing in the frontend consumes any of it: frontend/src/features holds auth and mis only, there is no /ask route, app-shell.tsx renders Ask and Explore as disabled nav items, api.ts has no chat method and still types runMisStatement as the pre-task-1 response, and frontend/package.json has no charting library. The assistant answers over HTTP and no human can see it.
new_abstractions: An assistant feature directory and a response renderer that dispatches on seven ResponseClass values whose payload shapes differ - the first place in this frontend where one component must render fundamentally different response bodies.
An in-memory thread that survives internal navigation but never a reload, which is a deliberate non-persistence design rather than an omission.
The first charting dependency in the project, with an honest-fallback rule so an undrawable shape degrades to a table.
gaps: The contract could not render charts as written: decision 0007 requires recharts when charts are needed, but frontend/package.json has no recharts and neither it nor the root lockfile was in write scope, which was already using all ten budgeted paths.

The approved prototype makes Ask a live navigation destination while frontend/src/components/shell/app-shell.tsx:15 renders it disabled with no href; a standalone /ask reachable only from the docked panel does not match that surface, and neither the shell nor its test was in scope.

The stale-link proof was misplaced: frontend/src/lib/api.ts:102 types runMisStatement as MisStatementRunResponse rather than the MisStatementRouteResponse task 1 shipped, so a refresh-required response reaches StatementView lacking the fields it reads, and an ask-panel test cannot prove the statement route parsed the server-supplied selectors, posted them and replaced the report with the refusal.

'Every non-success shows message' contradicted the payload: informational responses are emitted with title, definition and suggestedQuestions and no message (backend/src/chat/chat.service.ts:115,125), so rendering only message yields a blank response or invites the client to invent one.

Prior turns were underspecified: AskPriorTurn requires a selection (contract/src/api.ts:122) and only a successful answer supplies one, so a hook could invent selections for clarification or error turns; and the direct API test asserted only the absence of conversationId rather than the exact allow-listed body.
contradictions: The contract promised a live functional check of the Success path while BEDROCK_MODEL_ID had no value anywhere and MockLlmProvider only ever returns a clarification - so the check as written could not have been run.

The contract required the prototype's Suggested chip row on the empty state, but the backend supplies suggestedQuestions only after an informational answer and a successful answer's chips are interpretation chips, not prompts - so the first chips had no server source.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aas-c2 adds recharts per decision 0007, with frontend/package.json and the lockfile in scope and an explicit honest-fallback rule across kpi, line, bar, pie and table.
REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aas-c1 makes Ask a live shell destination and brings app-shell.tsx and its test into scope.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aas-c3 widens the api client's statement return type to the route union, branches mis-report-view.tsx on the refresh-required outcome, and moves that required leaf to mis-report-view.test.tsx.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aas-c4 states that the seven classes do not share a shape and handles informational, clarification and the four message-bearing failures separately, with a required leaf for the informational payload.
REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-aas-c5 restricts prior turns to successful turns and requires the api leaf to assert the exact request body.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - a model id is supplied, so the live Success check is expected to run for real. Verified after the round: loadConfig resolves llmProvider bedrock, region ap-south-1 and a set modelId from a machine-local env file, and a real Bedrock call returned kind 'selection' rather than the mock's clarification.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - the active thread is carried in in-memory app state across 'Open in Ask', so the control expands the conversation; a direct visit to /ask and any reload start fresh, so nothing durable is created and decision 0028 holds. Rejected: separate docked and page threads as the prototype draws them, which would silently lose the question just asked.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - the Suggested row is seeded with 3F-specific prompts rather than generic ones. Because that choice risks a chip returning 'unsupported', the criterion binds the seeds to the REGISTERED CATALOG - the governed-financial and mis-statement measures over the proven DUB slice - so every seeded chip is answerable, and server-supplied suggestedQuestions replace them when they arrive.
open_items: Non-blocking - the configured Bedrock model is mistral.mistral-large-3-675b-instruct, not a Claude model. Decision 0027 fixes the provider and region, not the model family, so this is compliant as written; answer quality rides on it and it is recorded here so nobody is surprised.
Non-blocking - the machine-local env file also sets BEDROCK_MODEL_ID_2, which config.ts does not read. It is inert.

Non-blocking - no 3F office or plant location is recorded anywhere in docs/; ap-south-1 was chosen from the code's existing default plus decision 0003's India-residency line. The human has not confirmed a residency requirement, and 0027 should be amended if one exists.

rounds.question: **The one I've been carrying.** `BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` has no default and no fallback, and `MockLlmProvider` only ever returns a clarification — it cannot select. So without a model id the assistant's *success* path cannot be exercised at all: not in this task's functional check, and not in a client demo. Everything else (clarification, the seven outcome classes, both surfaces, the report link's unavailable arm) is checkable without it.
options: I'll supply a model id — plan for a real check (Recommended)
No model id yet — record Success as blocked
Hold this task until the model id exists
rounds.chosen: I'll supply a model id — plan for a real check (Recommended)

rounds.question: The grill asked what "Open in Ask" does to the conversation. The prototype keeps separate message stores for the docked panel and the page, so following the control would discard the thread you were in. Decision 0028 forbids durable history, so whatever we choose lives in memory only.
options: Carry the thread across the control (Recommended)
Separate threads, as the prototype draws it
rounds.chosen: Carry the thread across the control (Recommended)
